topics.name: Questions with Have / Does / Are / Can and wh-words
Present perfect with ever, never, since, for
Modals of deduction (must, can't, must have)

options: Does your brother play the guitar?
Does your brother plays the guitar?
Do your brother play the guitar?
questions.rule: Use does with a singular subject, and after does the verb is in the base form: play.

options: Have you ever saw a rainbow at night?
Have you ever seen a rainbow at night?
Did you ever seen a rainbow at night?
questions.rule: Present perfect = have + past participle: Have you ever seen...?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After do/does in a question, the main verb is in the base form: Do the hands ... move?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Present perfect = has + past participle: has never visited.
A positive sentence with is takes a negative tag with is: isn't it?
Your sister is singular, and like is a base verb, so the question starts with Does.
Present perfect question: Have + subject + ever + past participle.

chat: Have you seen my blue pen?
options: No, I haven't seen it today.
No, I didn't seen it today.
No, I haven't saw it today.
questions.rule: Answer in the same tense: haven't + past participle = haven't seen.

questions.source: Your grandfather has seen a tiger.
options: Have your grandfather seen a tiger?
Has your grandfather saw a tiger?
Has your grandfather seen a tiger?
questions.rule: Move the helper has before the subject. The participle seen stays.

options: The garden hose is new, is it?
The garden hose is new, doesn't it?
The garden hose is new, isn't it?
questions.rule: Positive sentence with is takes a negative tag: isn't it?

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct question tag.
questions.rule: The tag repeats the helper can and turns it negative: can't he?

options: Why don't the bus stop here?
Why doesn't the bus stops here?
Why doesn't the bus stop here?
questions.rule: Singular the bus takes doesn't, followed by the base verb stop.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: She lives is simple present, singular, so the tag uses does: doesn't she?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Use for with a length of time (five years) and since with a starting point (2019).

questions.before: The lights are on, so Asha
questions.rule: The lights are a strong clue, so use must + base verb for a sure guess: must be. Never must to or is must.
In a statement use never (not ever) for 'not at any time': I have never eaten.
Wh-question: How often + does + subject + base verb.

options: Yes, it arrived an hour ago.
Yes, it has arrived an hour ago.
Yes, it arrive an hour ago.
questions.rule: With a finished past time like an hour ago, use the simple past: it arrived.

chat: You're coming to the match, aren't you?
options: Yes, I do. You will save me a seat, won't you?
Yes, I am. You will save me a seat, won't you?
Yes, I am. You will save me a seat, don't you?
questions.rule: Short answer matches are coming: Yes, I am. The tag for will is won't you?

questions.source: Neha has seen the new film.
options: Neha has not saw the new film.
Neha does not has seen the new film.
Neha has not seen the new film.
questions.rule: Put not after has. The past participle seen stays.

options: Ravi must has left early; his bag is not here.
Ravi must have left early; his bag is not here.
Ravi must have leave early; his bag is not here.
questions.rule: Deduction about the past: must have + past participle = must have left.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Does already carries the -s, so the main verb is the base form: does ... buy.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Nobody is negative, so the tag is positive, and it uses they with have: have they?
The wet ground is strong evidence, so use must have + past participle: must have rained (no to after must).

questions.before: Arjun has worked at this bakery
questions.rule: With the present perfect, use since + a starting point (a year, a date).

questions.prompt: Make a suggestion with a question tag.
questions.rule: A suggestion with Let's always takes the tag shall we?

chat: Where is your brother? His shoes are gone.
options: He must have gone to the park.
He must had gone to the park.
He must have went to the park.
questions.rule: Deduction about the past: must have + past participle. The participle of go is gone.

chat: I went to Mumbai last weekend.
options: Really? What did you saw there?
Really? What you did see there?
Really? What did you see there?
questions.rule: Past wh-question: What + did + subject + base verb: What did you see?

options: Rina never misses school, does she?
Rina never misses school, doesn't she?
Rina never misses school, did she?
questions.rule: Never makes the sentence negative, so the tag is positive: does she?

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Rani is singular: has never tried. After does, use the base verb like.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct question tag.
options: The children played well yesterday, didn't they?
The children played well yesterday, don't they?
The children played well yesterday, did they?
questions.rule: Played is simple past and positive, so the tag is didn't they?

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
questions.rule: A finished time like in 2022 needs the simple past (visited), not the present perfect.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Can't have + past participle shows something impossible in the past: can't have broken.
Neither of takes a singular verb, and present perfect is has + past participle: has seen.
Present perfect question: Has + subject + past participle; yet comes at the end.

options: No, it can't be my; mine is red.
No, it can't be mine; my is red.
No, it can't be mine; mine is red.
questions.rule: Use the possessive pronoun mine when no noun follows: it can't be mine; mine is red.

chat: Have you finished the book I lent you?
options: Yes, I have finished it last night. It was brilliant!
Yes, I finish it last night. It was brilliant!
Yes, I finished it last night. It was brilliant!
questions.rule: Last night is a finished time, so use the simple past: I finished it.

questions.prompt: Make a wh-question to get the words in brackets as the answer.
questions.source: Meera has lived in Nashik (for six years).
options: How long Meera has lived in Nashik?
How long has Meera lived in Nashik?
How long has Meera live in Nashik?
questions.rule: For six years answers How long. Then put has before the subject: How long has Meera lived?

questions.prompt: Change into the present perfect tense.
questions.rule: Present perfect = has + past participle. The participle of read is read.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Present perfect: Have you ever been. Plural tea gardens takes are, matching the tag aren't they.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct question tag.
options: I am late again, am not I?
I am late again, aren't I?
I am late again, isn't I?
questions.rule: The tag for I am is the special form aren't I?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Hardly makes the sentence negative, so the tag is positive, and anyone takes they: did they?
After a negative word like Seldom at the start, the helper comes before the subject: Seldom have I read.
Deduction about the past: must have + past participle = must have eaten.

chat: Why is Rohan's seat empty? He is never late.
options: He must have missed the bus.
He must have miss the bus.
questions.rule: A guess about the past uses must have + past participle: must have missed.

questions.source: Has anyone ever seen a needle wink?
options: No one has never seen a needle wink.
No one have ever seen a needle wink.
No one has ever seen a needle wink.
questions.rule: The rhetorical question means 'nobody'. Use No one has ever (no double negative), with singular has.

questions.source: I am sure Meena did not take your book.
options: Meena can't have took your book.
Meena can't have taken your book.
Meena must have taken your book.
questions.rule: Being sure something did not happen = can't have + past participle: can't have taken.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: must have gone (past participle); two ... bushes have been (plural); he always sleeps (singular, present habit).

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: After does use the base verb fly. My friend and I is plural: have wondered.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Two years ago needs the simple past: I went. The subject the bark is singular: was.
